findings.text: `_rearm_session_follower` is a near-verbatim twin of `_ask_session_host_for_follower` at the same file's line 732 -- same `_request_host_follower` guard, same WATCHER_LOAD_BOUND_SECONDS deadline, same 0.1 s poll -- so the capability "ask this session's host and wait, bounded" now has two bodies that will drift; a single helper taking the answer predicate would carry both callers, and the plan named the existing function as the mechanism this section routes through.

the re-arm names the run's session (`record["session"]`) while `_request_host_follower` and `_session_host_child_pid` resolve the FIFO and census from the calling Claude process (`_session_host_owner` at reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:582), so a resume issued from a session other than the run's dispatcher writes a request for another session's pair to its own host, which spawns a follower writing into the caller's pane and returns follower_rearmed True while the resumed run's own session stays unfollowed.
